dispatch_anomaly.charter_stop_rule: TERMINATE the charter after either outcome; never re-dispatch it with the same charter_version
dispatch_anomaly.handling: This cycle did NOT open a new charter cycle and did not issue a new claim. It absorbed the duplicate dispatch by independently re-verifying the accepted numbers and repairing the four defects the accepted gate recorded as non-binding advisories. A duplicate dispatch is still a factory-level condition: this component now needs an independent AUDIT of run 38970902524, not another cycle.

independent_reverification.method: Fresh recomputation from origin data, not from the committed artifact: the bundles' issued counter labels re-scored with the vendored frozen rubric, compared to LABEL_HALF.json as a MULTISET over full verdict tuples, and the candidate re-run on the same 65 rows.
independent_reverification.verdict: ACCEPTED OUTCOME A CLAIM IS SOUND AS STATED

repairs.defect: _compare_to_accepted keyed both sides by decision_id into plain dicts. 4 decision_ids occur twice in the 65-row population, so 65 rows collapsed to 61 keys and reproduced_byte_identical_verdicts was asserted on 61 rows; a disagreement between the two copies of a duplicated id would have been invisible.
repairs.impact_if_unrepaired: the reproduction proof covered 61 of 65 rows
repairs.fix: multiset (Counter) comparison over (bundle, decision_id, counter_status, primary_defect_class, reason_code, supported), plus coverage_is_full_population and explicit duplicate-id reporting

repairs.defect: STATUS_TO_LABEL.get(proposed, LABEL_LIMITING) turned any unrecognised issued counter_status into the label 'limiting', so the component could name a polarity the row never carried, which its own claim ceiling forbids.
repairs.impact_if_unrepaired: an adapter feeding a status outside the six documented values would ship a fabricated 'limiting' label
repairs.fix: an unmapped or empty counter_status now yields a COUNTED abstention with reason unmapped_proposed_status (uncertainty 0.9), audited as criterion vi_proposed_status_mappable; the check is placed LAST in the gate so the four frozen precedence steps and their accepted counts are untouched by construction
repairs.behaviour_preservation_proof: all 65 rows carry candidate-limiting (45), candidate-contrary (11) or contrary_or_exception (9), all mapped, so the path is unreachable on the measured population; proven by test_repair_population_preserved.py::test_unmapped_status_path_is_unreachable_on_this_population

repairs.defect: REPORT.md stated the swapped-evidence control abstains with no_intent_marker
repairs.fix: corrected in place with a visible correction note; the true frozen-precedence reason is pivot_absent (all 5 control rows), pinned by test_repair_38970902524.py
repairs.note: both controls scored 0/5 and abstained, so only the stated reason was wrong; the non-vacuity result is unchanged

repairs.defect: run_head_to_head.main() resolved the repo root with three dirname() hops, so --rules defaulted to <repo>/frontier/results/.../RULES_LABEL.json and the documented module invocation crashed with FileNotFoundError before scoring. Only the explicit-path test call ever worked.
repairs.fix: four hops; and the default --out now targets the repair-cycle artifact so a CLI run can never overwrite the accepted HEAD_TO_HEAD.json
repairs.verified: the documented invocation was re-run end to end and wrote results/frontier/frontier-counter-anchor-classifier/HEAD_TO_HEAD_R2_38970902524.json

also_corrected: the decide_label docstring listed the frozen precedence with polarity-inversion at step 3 and procedural-formula at step 4; the frozen RULES_LABEL.json order is the reverse, which is what the code and the vendored scorer both apply

tests.fixture_provenance: the 5 rows the component really emits on the served packet, copied verbatim, so repair tests mutate real rows instead of invented ones
